blocks.orig: Once you’ve booked your dream safari in Tanzania or your beach escape to Zanzibar, there’s one important step between you and your African adventure: getting your visa! The good news is that it’s straightforward, and we’re here to guide you through it.
blocks.html: With your dream safari in Tanzania or your beach break on Zanzibar booked, only one key task stands between you and your African adventure: arranging your visa! Happily, the process is simple, and we’ll help you every step of the way.

blocks.orig: There are two ways to obtain your Tanzania visa: apply online before you travel (eVisa) or get it on arrival at the airport. The main difference is timing, not outcome. With an eVisa, you receive approval before you travel, whereas a visa on arrival is completed at the airport. On arrival, there are separate queues for eVisa holders and visa-on-arrival applicants, so everyone still waits – just in different queues.
blocks.html: You can get your Tanzania visa in one of two ways: by applying online ahead of your trip (eVisa) or by obtaining it at the airport when you land. What differs is the timing, not the result. An eVisa is approved before you leave home, while a visa on arrival is handled at the airport itself. Once you land, eVisa holders and visa-on-arrival applicants join separate queues, so you will wait either way – simply in a different line.

blocks.orig: One of our travel consultants regularly travels between Germany and Tanzania and has used both visa options many times. Her experience is simple: neither option is better for everyone. The eVisa offers peace of mind, as your approval is sorted before departure, though it can take on average 3 to 10 working days. The visa on arrival involves less planning before you fly, but means handling the entire process after landing. In the end, it comes down to preference…prepare in advance, or keep things flexible until you arrive.
blocks.html: A member of our travel team often flies between Germany and Tanzania and has tried both visa routes many times. Her conclusion is straightforward: no single option suits everyone. With the eVisa, you can relax because approval is arranged before you depart, although it takes 3 to 10 working days on average. The visa on arrival needs less preparation before your flight, but you then deal with the whole procedure after touching down. Ultimately, it is a matter of taste…get ready ahead of time, or stay flexible until you land.

blocks.orig: The online route gives you peace of mind. You’ll arrive in Tanzania with your Visa Grant Notice already in hand, ready to get that stamp in your passport and start your adventure. This is especially valuable if you’re travelling with children or in a group.
blocks.html: Applying online lets you travel without worries. When you reach Tanzania, you’ll already have your Visa Grant Notice with you, so all that remains is the stamp in your passport before your adventure begins. This is particularly useful when you travel with children or as a group.

blocks.orig: The main advantage is knowing everything is sorted before you board the plane. Plus, if you’re travelling with kids and only one parent is going, a written permission document from the other parent is required – in English. This is not something you want to find out upon arrival at the Tanzanian airport!
blocks.html: The biggest benefit is knowing that everything is arranged before you get on the plane. What’s more, when children travel with just one parent, written permission from the other parent is needed – in English. You would not want to discover this only when you land at the Tanzanian airport!

blocks.orig: Timing matters: Apply 3-4 weeks before your departure date. This ensures your visa is processed on time and provides a buffer for any delays or issues.
blocks.html: Get the timing right: Submit your application 3-4 weeks ahead of your departure. That way your visa is processed in time and you have some leeway if there are delays or problems.

blocks.orig: The cost: It’s 50 USD or 50 EUR whether you apply online or at the airport. Payment can be made in cash or by credit card, though credit card payments may sometimes experience delays. The ordinary visa is valid for up to 90 days and is intended for a single entry.
blocks.html: What it costs: You pay 50 USD or 50 EUR, regardless of whether you apply online or at the airport. You can pay in cash or by credit card, although card payments are occasionally delayed. The ordinary visa allows a single entry and is valid for a maximum of 90 days.

blocks.orig: US citizens, take note: You’ll need to apply for a multiple-entry visa costing 100 USD instead of the standard 50 USD single-entry visa. This requirement is due to a bilateral agreement between the US and Tanzania, meaning US passport holders are not eligible for the 50 USD single-entry visa, even for a one-time visit. The visa is valid for one year, though a single stay cannot exceed 90 days.
blocks.html: A note for US citizens: Instead of the standard 50 USD single-entry visa, you’ll have to apply for a multiple-entry visa at 100 USD. This rule stems from a bilateral agreement between the US and Tanzania, so holders of a US passport cannot get the 50 USD single-entry visa, even if they visit only once. The visa remains valid for one year, but any one stay may not be longer than 90 days.

blocks.orig: Only use the official website: This is crucial. Apply only through the official Tanzania immigration website. Numerous other websites will either scam you or charge hefty service fees for something you can easily do for yourself for free.
blocks.html: Stick to the official website: This really matters. Submit your application exclusively via the official immigration website of Tanzania. Plenty of other sites will either defraud you or add steep service charges for a task you can easily complete yourself at no extra cost.

blocks.orig: Passport validity: Your passport must be valid for at least six months upon return from Tanzania.
blocks.html: How long your passport must be valid: On your return from Tanzania, your passport needs at least six months of remaining validity.

blocks.orig: One visa covers it all: Whether you’re heading to the mainland, Zanzibar, or both, you only need one visa for Tanzania.
blocks.html: A single visa is enough: You need just one visa for Tanzania, whether you’re visiting the mainland, Zanzibar or both.

blocks.orig: Travelling with children: If kids are travelling with only one parent, a written permission document from the other parent is required.
blocks.html: Children on the trip: When children travel with just one parent, written permission from the other parent must be provided.

blocks.orig: When applying for your Tanzania visa, keep in mind that the system may work differently from what you’re used to. The website can go down for short periods, uploads may fail, or payments may not go through on the first try.
blocks.html: As you apply for your Tanzania visa, bear in mind that the system might not behave the way you expect. The site can be offline for brief spells, uploads sometimes fail, and a payment may not succeed at the first attempt.

blocks.orig: Stay calm and think “TIA” – This Is Africa. Usually, trying again later or switching browsers (Mozilla Firefox or Google Chrome work best) solves the issue. One of our clients had to upload documents three times due to timeouts, but after a short wait, everything went through without a problem.
blocks.html: Keep your cool and remember “TIA” – This Is Africa. In most cases the problem is solved by trying again a little later or using another browser (Mozilla Firefox or Google Chrome work best). One client of ours needed three attempts to upload documents because of timeouts, yet after a brief wait it all went through smoothly.

blocks.orig: Both the eVisa and visa on arrival work well. The online option takes a bit more time and requires extra information, but it gives you control and peace of mind – great for those who like to have everything sorted in advance. Visa on arrival is simpler, needing just your passport (and sometimes a return ticket). It’s perfect if you want to skip online forms or don’t have a credit card. Whichever route you choose, make sure to check all requirements, especially passport validity and any documentation needed for children.
blocks.html: The eVisa and the visa on arrival both do the job. Applying online asks for a little more time and extra details, but it puts you in control and lets you travel relaxed – ideal if you prefer everything arranged beforehand. The visa on arrival is more straightforward, as you only need your passport (and occasionally a return ticket). It suits you well if you would rather avoid online forms or have no credit card. Whichever option you pick, check every requirement, in particular passport validity and any paperwork needed for children.
